title: Maximum Distance Between Unequal Words in Array II
summary: Given an array of strings, determine the greatest distance between two different indices where the strings at these indices are not identical.
statement: Given an array of strings, determine the greatest distance between two different indices where the strings at these indices are not identical. The distance is calculated as the difference between the indices plus one. Return this maximum distance, or 0 if no such pair exists.
constraints: words contains up to 100,000 nonempty lowercase strings.
The inclusive distance between indices i and j is |i-j|+1.
Return the maximum distance whose endpoint words differ, or zero if every word is equal.
hints: At least one endpoint of an optimal unequal pair can be moved to an array boundary.
Compare every word with the first and last words and measure the corresponding inclusive distance.
Take the largest valid first-to-index or index-to-last candidate.
If an optimal pair uses neither boundary, a boundary word must differ from at least one of its endpoint words and yields no shorter a span.
editorial: If an optimal pair uses neither boundary, a boundary word must differ from at least one of its endpoint words and yields no shorter a span.

tests.explanation: The first and last words differ, so their inclusive distance is three.
Indices one and four contain different words and have inclusive distance four.
